blindSummary: For trans visitors this country presents extreme risk. Same-sex conduct is not named in the criminal code — but one provision prohibits "decadent culture" and broad provisions on "obscene activities" give authorities unlimited discretion; reported incidents of criminalisation and even execution for homosexuality exist. The concept of gender identity simply does not exist in public life (sexual minorities are "denied as a concept", in the words of one foreign broadcaster's reporting). Tourists are under constant escort and surveillance; any nonconforming presentation or discovered digital material risks detention in the world's most totalitarian system.
blindOutOfScope: Data scarcity reflects totalitarian control; traveller surveillance is universal.
blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): no laws appear to penalise consensual same-sex acts in the criminal code (in force since 1950, updated 2009), but one provision prohibits 'decadent culture' (including sexual video recordings) and another prohibits collective 'obscene activities'; the state denied the existence of same-sex activity in 2014; an unconfirmed 2011 report claimed execution of a lesbian couple; no freedom of assembly.

Legal-information platform overview (May 2026): this country has no law explicitly criminalising same-sex activity, but broad provisions on 'decadent culture' and 'obscene activities' give authorities wide discretion; the government publicly denies that LGBT people exist; people who have escaped the country describe a deeply repressive reality.

A foreign public broadcaster's foreign-language service (Oct 2024): a feature asking whether same-sex love exists at all in this country, on the near-total erasure of its sexual minorities; interviews with a writer who escaped the country; notes new laws (a language-purification law, a youth-education law, a law rejecting 'reactionary thought and culture') further tightening control; the state does not even acknowledge the concept.

A foreign government's 2022 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - the totalitarian regime's pervasive abuses; the report notes no specific law criminalising same-sex conduct, but the regime's total control leaves no space for LGBT life.

A foreign government's 2020 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - no reliable information on LGBT persons; the regime's repression of all civil society is the dominant human-rights reality.
A cable-news report (Apr 2017): a defector's account of what it is like to be a gay man from this country — concealment, punishment and escape.

State news agency commentary (April 2014): this country's state news agency attacked the chair of a UN commission of inquiry - personally insulting him by reference to his decades-long homosexuality and claiming that homosexuality 'can never be found' in this country - an official statement of the regime's homophobia.
